realLifeExampleSummary: Dasselbe Produkt kann als 90 % fettfrei oder 10 % Fett beschrieben werden, obwohl die Zahlen mathematisch dasselbe ausdrücken.
coverVisualThesis: Two mathematically equivalent descriptions of the same product are shown side by side so the viewer immediately sees that identical information can be presented from different angles.

scenes.speechSection: Warum klingt dieselbe Entscheidung plötzlich besser, nur weil dieselben Folgen anders beschrieben werden?
scenes.viewerTakeaway: Equivalent information can feel different when its presentation changes.
scenes.observableEvidence: The same illustrated food product appears twice with equivalent positive and negative numeric descriptions while all product details remain identical.
scenes.representationReason: The hook is about two equivalent presentations, so a direct side-by-side comparison communicates the mechanism faster than a character scene.
scenes.dominantRelation: Same product and same numbers, two different descriptions.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: Do not use a literal picture frame just because the topic is Framing.

scenes.viewerTakeaway: The viewer learns the name of the effect.
scenes.observableEvidence: The exact term is integrated into the same illustrated world beside two equivalent information cards with different emphasis.
scenes.representationReason: This beat simply names the concept, so exact text is clearer than another behavioral scene.
scenes.dominantRelation: Concept term plus two equivalent but differently emphasized information cards.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: Do not use a literal picture frame.

scenes.speechSection: Vereinfacht gesagt: Die Formulierung kann beeinflussen, wie wir dieselbe Information bewerten.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: Wording changes which part of identical information becomes salient.
scenes.observableEvidence: One neutral circular data graphic is duplicated: one version visually emphasizes the large retained portion, the other emphasizes the smaller lost portion, while the underlying proportions stay identical.
scenes.representationReason: A simple mechanism shows unchanged data with changed emphasis more clearly than a person reacting.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: Do not use a literal picture frame.

scenes.speechSection: Ein Produkt mit „90 % fettfrei“ kann attraktiver wirken als dasselbe Produkt mit „10 % Fett“.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: Attribute framing can change evaluation even when the numbers are equivalent.
scenes.observableEvidence: Two identical illustrated yogurt-style packages sit side by side; only the front wording differs between the mathematically equivalent descriptions.
scenes.representationReason: The packaging wording itself carries the example, so full characters would only add clutter.
scenes.dominantRelation: Identical product, equivalent labels, different emphasis.

scenes.speechSection: Die Zahlen sind gleich, aber der positive oder negative Rahmen lenkt Aufmerksamkeit auf unterschiedliche Aspekte.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: The same quantity can direct attention toward different parts depending on wording.
scenes.observableEvidence: The same 90/10 circular proportion appears twice; one side highlights the 90-part majority while the other highlights the 10-part minority, with identical geometry.
scenes.representationReason: A direct visual equivalence check makes the unchanged numbers obvious without needing a human reaction.
scenes.dominantRelation: Same 90/10 proportion, attention directed to opposite parts.

scenes.speechSection: Berühmt wurde dieser Effekt durch Arbeiten von Amos Tversky und Daniel Kahneman Anfang der 1980er Jahre.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: The classic framing research belongs to the early 1980s decision-research context.
scenes.observableEvidence: An early-1980s behavioral research room with paper questionnaires, pencils, simple probability-choice cards, a period desk lamp and institutional furniture; no portraits or readable documents.
scenes.representationReason: The research era is the point, so period environment and materials establish it more efficiently than invented portraits.
scenes.dominantRelation: Period research materials arranged for a decision experiment.

scenes.speechSection: In ihrem bekannten Entscheidungsproblem wurden mathematisch vergleichbare Folgen einmal als Gewinne und einmal als Verluste beschrieben.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: The classic task presented equivalent outcomes using gain and loss descriptions.
scenes.observableEvidence: A single experiment table shows two mirrored decision layouts built from the same set of 600 small person-tokens: one layout groups the preserved tokens, the other groups the lost tokens; the quantities match.
scenes.representationReason: The equivalence of gain and loss descriptions is structural, so a mirrored outcome layout is clearer than another talking-person scene.
scenes.dominantRelation: Same total outcome represented once as preserved and once as lost.

scenes.speechSection: Bei der Gewinn-Formulierung wurde häufiger die sichere Möglichkeit gewählt.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: In the classic gain frame, the sure option was chosen more often.
scenes.observableEvidence: In the same early-1980s lab, one participant stickman studies two choice cards and decisively places a hand on the visually certain option while the probabilistic option remains untouched.
scenes.representationReason: The human choice itself is the evidence here, so a participant selecting the sure option is necessary.
scenes.dominantRelation: Participant selects sure option over risky alternative.

scenes.speechSection: Bei der Verlust-Formulierung verschob sich die Wahl häufiger in Richtung der riskanteren Möglichkeit.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: In the classic loss frame, choices shifted more toward the risky option.
scenes.observableEvidence: A second participant in the same period lab chooses the probabilistic option card while the certain-loss option remains beside it; posture and hand placement make the riskier selection unambiguous.
scenes.representationReason: This beat concerns an observed choice shift, so the participant's visible selection is the clearest evidence.
scenes.dominantRelation: Participant selects risky option over certain-loss alternative.

scenes.speechSection: Das bedeutet aber nicht, dass Worte jede Entscheidung beliebig steuern.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: Framing does not produce one guaranteed response.
scenes.observableEvidence: Three parallel miniature decision setups show the same wording treatment but different outcomes: one hand chooses left, one chooses right, and one remains undecided.
scenes.representationReason: Three visibly different responses to the same presentation directly refute an automatic-control interpretation.

scenes.speechSection: Meta-Analysen zeigen Framing-Effekte, aber ihre Stärke hängt deutlich von Aufgabe, Formulierung und Kontext ab.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: Research finds framing effects, but their magnitude varies across tasks and contexts.
scenes.observableEvidence: A research desk is covered with many differently shaped study cards, outcome diagrams and context-specific materials arranged around a central stack, with visibly varied effect marks rather than one uniform result.
scenes.representationReason: A varied research-workspace composition communicates heterogeneity across studies without inventing a single universal human reaction.
scenes.dominantRelation: Many study contexts produce visibly non-uniform result patterns.

scenes.speechSection: Außerdem gibt es verschiedene Arten von Framing: Risiko-, Eigenschafts- und Ziel-Framing funktionieren nicht identisch.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: Framing includes distinct categories rather than one single mechanism.
scenes.observableEvidence: One coherent illustrated three-part typology: a chance-choice card for risk, a product attribute card for attribute framing, and a goal/outcome path for goal framing.
scenes.representationReason: This beat explicitly names three categories, so a compact labeled typology is the clearest form.
scenes.dominantRelation: Three distinct framing categories shown as different visual mechanisms.

scenes.speechSection: Framing ist deshalb kein zuverlässiger Manipulationsknopf, mit dem man Menschen immer in dieselbe Richtung lenkt.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: Framing is not a guaranteed manipulation switch.
scenes.observableEvidence: Three stickman adults receive the same differently worded choice card: one accepts, one rejects, and one sets it aside, each with distinct posture and hand action.
scenes.representationReason: Different human responses to the same frame are the evidence that there is no guaranteed direction of control.
scenes.dominantRelation: Same framed message, three different responses.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: Do not show a literal manipulation button or puppet strings.

scenes.speechSection: Praktisch hilft ein Gegencheck: Formuliere dieselbe Information einmal als Gewinn und einmal als Verlust.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: A practical check is to rewrite the same fact in both directions.
scenes.observableEvidence: An illustrated notebook lies open with two clean columns containing the same neutral data card rewritten under the headings GAIN and LOSS in German; one pen rests between them.
scenes.representationReason: The practical action is a writing/reframing exercise, so the notebook itself should carry the frame.
scenes.dominantRelation: Same fact deliberately rewritten in two opposite directions.

scenes.speechSection: Wenn sich deine Bewertung stark verändert, reagierst du möglicherweise teilweise auf die Darstellung und nicht nur auf die Fakten.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: A noticeable preference shift after rewording can reveal sensitivity to presentation.
scenes.observableEvidence: One adult stickman sits with the two rewritten cards side by side, pauses with a hand between them, then looks back to the identical neutral data sheet underneath both.
scenes.representationReason: The reflective comparison between one's own two evaluations is a human behavior beat, so a single character is useful.
scenes.dominantRelation: Person compares two reactions against the same underlying facts.

scenes.speechSection: Die Information kann gleich bleiben – aber der Blickwinkel verändert, was zuerst ins Auge fällt.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: The underlying information can stay constant while attention shifts.
scenes.observableEvidence: A two-sided information card is shown mid-turn: both sides contain the same 90/10 proportion, but one side visually emphasizes the large portion and the other the small portion.
scenes.representationReason: The ending is about unchanged information with changed emphasis, so one transforming object closes the idea cleanly.
scenes.dominantRelation: Same data card, opposite emphasis, unchanged proportions.
